title: Interactive Water Cycle Visualization
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D water cycle visualization using Three.js and GLTFLoader. The scene should educate users about the water cycle stages.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 15, 30) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light simulating the sun at position (20, 30, 10) with intensity 1.2, colored #FDB813 (warm yellow).
- Create a ground plane (40x40) textured with a green/brown color representing terrain, slightly undulating.
- Create a blue semi-transparent water body (a flat box or plane) on the left side of the scene at position (-10, 0.1, 0) sized 15x0.3x20, color #2196F3 with opacity 0.7.
- Create a mountain/hill on the right side using a ConeGeometry(5, 10, 8) at position (10, 5, 0), colored #8B7355.
- Add clouds: 3 white semi-transparent sphere clusters at y=18, positions (-5,18,0), (0,18,3), (5,18,-2). Each cloud is a group of 3-4 merged spheres, white color, opacity 0.8.
- Load the 'WaterBottle.glb' model using GLTFLoader. Place it at position (0, 0.5, 8) with scale (5, 5, 5). This serves as a decorative/educational prop representing water containment.

## Water Cycle Particles
- Create a particle system for water droplets. Use small blue spheres (radius 0.1) managed in an array.
- The cycle has 4 phases: EVAPORATION, CONDENSATION, PRECIPITATION, COLLECTION.
- During EVAPORATION: particles rise from the water body surface (y: 0 to 18) with slight random horizontal drift. Particles should be light blue and semi-transparent.
- During CONDENSATION: particles cluster near clouds (y~18), change color to white/gray, and slowly merge toward cloud centers.
- During PRECIPITATION: particles fall from clouds as rain (y: 18 to 0), colored dark blue, with slight wind drift.
- During COLLECTION: particles flow along the ground toward the water body (moving in -x direction toward the lake).

## Animation & Controls
- The cycle auto-plays continuously by default. Each phase lasts 3 seconds (total cycle = 12 seconds).
- A 'Play/Pause' button (id='playPauseBtn') toggles animation. Display 'Pause' when playing, 'Play' when paused.
- A 'Next Phase' button (id='nextPhaseBtn') manually advances to the next phase.
- A 'Reset' button (id='resetBtn') resets to EVAPORATION phase and restarts.
- A speed slider (id='speedSlider', range 0.5 to 3.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) controls animation speed.
- Keyboard: press '1' for EVAPORATION, '2' for CONDENSATION, '3' for PRECIPITATION, '4' for COLLECTION to jump to that phase.
- Keyboard: press 'Space' to toggle play/pause.

## HUD / UI
- Display current phase name in a div (id='phaseLabel') at top center, large font, with phase-appropriate color (EVAPORATION=#FF6B35, CONDENSATION=#A0A0A0, PRECIPITATION=#1565C0, COLLECTION=#2E7D32).
- Display a cycle counter (id='cycleCounter') showing how many complete cycles have occurred.
- Display particle count (id='particleCount') showing active particles.
- Display elapsed time in current phase (id='phaseTimer') in seconds with 1 decimal.
- Add an info panel (id='infoPanel') that shows a 1-2 sentence educational description of the current phase.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- currentPhase: string ('EVAPORATION'|'CONDENSATION'|'PRECIPITATION'|'COLLECTION')
- phaseIndex: number (0-3)
- isPlaying: boolean
- speed: number (the speed multiplier)
- cycleCount: number (completed full cycles)
- particleCount: number (active particles in scene)
- phaseElapsed: number (seconds elapsed in current phase)
- sunIntensity: number (directional light intensity)
- waterBottleLoaded: boolean (true once GLB model is loaded)
- cloudCount: number (number of cloud groups)
- waterBodyVisible: boolean

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Particles must obey gravity during precipitation (accelerating downward). Evaporation particles rise with decreasing speed. All particle positions must remain within scene bounds (-25 to 25 on x/z, 0 to 22 on y). Particle count should be between 20-200 at any time during animation. Phase transitions should be smooth.
